Job Description
Electronics Data Systems Technicians maintain data link, tactical network, message-routing, digital production/projection, calibration, fiber optics, micro-
miniature module test and repair, computer-based, and peripheral computer systems; analyze equipment operation, establish computer and network
configurations, and troubleshoot and repair computer-based equipment to the lowest replaceable unit; execute casualty control procedures, restoring
operability for all assigned electronic equipment, recognizing mission criticality and redundancies within systems; perform administrative functions that
include updating casualty reporting messages, technical manuals, equipment maintenance records, and managing test equipment calibration requirements;
complete fiber optic and basic soldering repair, electrical safety checks, and test equipment calibration; and supervise personnel who conduct tool and test
equipment inventories, logistics support, and maintenance and testing of systems and equipment.

Electronics Technicians (ET) perform, supervise, coordinate, and manage the preventive and corrective maintenance, calibration, configuration, and alignment of cryptographic, radar, navigation, and Command, Control, Computer, Communication, and Intelligence (C4I) systems, utilizing test equipment and technical drawings. __________________________________________

Electronics Data Systems Technicians maintain data link, tactical network, message-routing, digital production/projection, calibration, fiber optics, micro- miniature module test and repair, computer-based, and peripheral computer systems; analyze equipment operation, establish computer and network configurations, and troubleshoot and repair computer-based equipment to the lowest replaceable unit; execute casualty control procedures, restoring operability for all assigned electronic equipment, recognizing mission criticality and redundancies within systems; perform administrative functions that include updating casualty reporting messages, technical manuals, equipment maintenance records, and managing test equipment calibration requirements; complete fiber optic and basic soldering repair, electrical safety checks, and test equipment calibration; and supervise personnel who conduct tool and test equipment inventories, logistics support, and maintenance and testing of systems and equipment.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
